newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Committee says Duma should reject 97 Russia budget.
newsitem.headline: Committee says Duma should reject 97 Russia budget.

text.p: Russia's 1997 budget, due to be discussed on Friday by the State Duma lower house of parliament, should be rejected in its current form, the head of parliament's budget committee Mikhail Zadornov said on Wednesday.
He told reporters the committee was unhappy with the revenue side of the draft and had doubts about proposed levels of tax collection.
"The committe, by an overwheleming majority, recommended the rejection of the budget," Zadornov said.
The draft envisages spending of 524.34 trillion roubles, revenues of 433.64 trillion and a deficit of 90.70 trillion, or 3.3 percent of GDP.

Zadornov said two members of the committee had recommended the budget be sent back to the government for reworking, but 25 said it should be sent to a reconciliation commission of the government and the Duma to see if a compromise could be reached.

Low tax collection has also plagued the 1996 budget and the State Tax Service has said the government collected only 45 percent of budgeted taxes in September while January-September collection was running at 75 percent of planned levels.
Zadornov said this was contributing to a growth in wage arrears. "The objective indicators show the situation is not improving, but worsening."
He said the government seemed ready to rework aspects of the budget dealing with revenue and spending.
